title: Component API entry
description: Schema for one component-api/<id>.json file. See component-api/README.md for the full field-by-field rationale, this file is the machine-checkable version of that same schema.

id.description: Stable slug, matches index.html's DATA array id and the same-named guidance-api/token-api entries. Never null.

summary.description: One plain-language sentence, no implementation detail, for someone who wants to know what the thing is before reading the technical description.

tagName.description: The real, registered custom element tag name, if one exists. null for none/missing kinds, and sometimes for modern/classic kinds where no distinct tag was ever registered. A dual-kind entry may record both real tags in one string (e.g. "button (classic) / moz-button (modern)").

description.description: One or two sentences, grounded in the actual source file, not a generic restatement of the component's name.

file.description: Path relative to the mozilla-central root. The primary source-of-truth file this JSON was derived from.

default.description: CEM's own field name. This attribute's real default value/state when not otherwise set. Omitted, not guessed, when source doesn't establish one explicitly.

figmaConfig.description: Whether this attribute is real user-facing configuration vs. internal/plumbing-only state. Omitted, not guessed, when genuinely unclear.

default.description: CEM's own field for this property's real literal value, used here for a property with no backing design token. Omitted, not guessed, when no such real default exists.

cssParts.description: CEM's own field name. Real `::part()` names found in the component's own shadow-DOM render output (or a shared base class it genuinely extends), for shadow-DOM components only. Acorn is mostly light-DOM by design, so most entries have none.

usage.description: A realistic, real-attribute usage example. Not a hypothetical.
